title: Trial Balance
outcomes: State what a trial balance is, why it is prepared and why it is a statement, not an account.
Prepare a trial balance by the total method, the balance method and the combined method.
Place each kind of balance on the correct side, including tricky items like returns, outstanding and prepaid expenses.
Explain which errors a trial balance cannot reveal and how a suspense account is used when it does not agree.

meta.exam_tip: "Redraft the trial balance" and "prepare a trial balance with capital as the balancing figure" are favourite short questions.

concepts.title: What a trial balance is
body: A list of all ledger accounts with their debit and credit totals or balances, prepared on a particular date. Because every debit has an equal credit, the two columns must agree.
Objectives: test the arithmetical accuracy of posting and balancing; give a summary of the ledger; and provide the base for preparing the financial statements.
It is a statement, not an account — it has no "To" and "By" and is not part of the double entry.
concepts.analogy: A class register check at the end of the day: if the boys plus girls do not equal the total, someone was counted wrongly. If it does match, it still does not prove everyone sat in the right seat.
concepts.work: In audit and accounting work the trial balance is the starting document. Each line is "mapped" to a line in the balance sheet or the profit and loss statement.

concepts.title: Three methods
body: Total method — write the total of each side of every account. Quick (no balancing needed), but long.
Balance method — write only the balance of each account on its side. This is the method used for preparing final accounts and in most exam questions.
Total-cum-balance method — show both totals and balances in four columns. Rarely used in practice because it is lengthy.

head: Account
Dr total (₹)
Cr total (₹)
blocks.title: Total method (each side of every account)

concepts.analogy: Total method shows every ball bowled; balance method shows only the final score.
concepts.work: Software prints the trial balance in the balance method by default; some also offer an "opening + Dr + Cr + closing" view, which is the combined method in a modern form.

concepts.title: Which side does it go on?
body: Debit side: assets, expenses, losses, drawings, debtors, purchases, sales returns, opening stock, prepaid expenses, accrued income.
Credit side: capital, liabilities, incomes, gains, creditors, sales, purchase returns, bank overdraft, outstanding expenses, income received in advance, provisions.
Closing stock normally appears outside the trial balance as an adjustment — unless it has already been adjusted (then it is shown on the debit side and purchases are reduced).
concepts.analogy: Ask: does the business own it or spend on it (debit), or does it owe it or earn it (credit)?
concepts.work: A prepaid rent shown on the credit side or a bank overdraft shown as an asset will make the balance sheet wrong even if totals somehow agree.

concepts.title: Limitations: agreement is not proof
body: These errors do not disturb the agreement: a transaction completely omitted; a wrong amount written in the journal and posted on both sides; posting to the wrong account but on the correct side (error of commission); wrong classification such as an asset debited to an expense (error of principle); and errors that cancel each other (compensating errors).
Errors that do cause a difference: posting on the wrong side, posting only one side, wrong totalling or balancing of an account, or omitting a balance from the trial balance.
concepts.analogy: A balanced scale tells you both pans weigh the same — not that you weighed the right things.
concepts.work: Auditors never rely on an agreed trial balance alone; they still test transactions with documents for exactly these hidden errors.

concepts.title: Suspense account
body: If the trial balance does not agree and the accounts must still be prepared, the difference is put to a Suspense Account so the totals agree temporarily.

As errors are found, rectifying entries are passed through the suspense account until it closes (Unit 6). A suspense balance left at the year end is shown in the balance sheet but should be investigated.
concepts.analogy: A "lost and found" box: you park the unexplained amount there until you find where it belongs.
concepts.work: An unexplained suspense balance is a serious audit observation — it means the books contain unidentified errors.

jobs.title: Mapping the trial balance for the audit file
jobs.situation: The client sends a trial balance with 240 ledger accounts. Your senior asks you to map each line to the financial statement heads and to flag anything odd.
steps: Check that the trial balance totals agree and that the opening balances match last year's audited figures.
Map each ledger to a statement line (e.g. Sundry debtors → Trade receivables).
Flag balances on the "wrong" side: debit balances in creditors, credit balances in expenses, any suspense balance.
Prepare a lead schedule for each head that the audit team will test.
jobs.takeaway: Knowing the normal side of every balance is the fastest way to spot problems in a real trial balance.
jobs.think: An expense account like Repairs shows a credit balance. What could have happened?
jobs.answer: A refund or reversal was larger than the expenses recorded, an income was posted to Repairs, or an entry was posted on the wrong side — each needs checking.

jobs.title: Month-end close in a company
jobs.role: Junior accountant in a finance team
jobs.situation: Your team closes the books on the third working day. The controller asks for the trial balance and an explanation of any suspense balance.
steps: Run the trial balance from the system and confirm it agrees.
Review suspense or "clearing" accounts and trace every open item to its source.
Pass correcting entries and rerun the trial balance before reporting.
jobs.takeaway: Suspense accounts should be cleared every month — old unexplained items become very hard to trace.
jobs.think: Why is it risky to leave a small suspense balance of ₹300 unexplained?
jobs.answer: It may be the net of two large errors that almost cancel each other — for example ₹50,300 and ₹50,000 — so the real misstatement could be much bigger.

mcqs.explain: It lists balances to test accuracy; it is not part of the double entry.

mcqs.q: Which item appears on the credit side of a trial balance?
mcqs.explain: Outstanding salary is a liability. The other three are debits.

mcqs.q: Which error will NOT affect the agreement of the trial balance?
options: Credit sale to Mohan posted to Sohan's account
Cash received from a debtor posted only to Cash account
Rent paid posted to the credit of Rent account
mcqs.explain: Posting to the wrong account on the correct side (error of commission) keeps debits equal to credits.

mcqs.q: Total debit balances are ₹6,48,000 and credit balances other than capital are ₹4,12,500. Capital is:
If the trial balance does not agree, the difference is temporarily placed in:
mcqs.explain: A suspense account holds the difference until the errors are located.

mcqs.q: Under which method of preparing a trial balance is balancing of accounts NOT needed?
mcqs.explain: The total method uses each side's total; balances are not required.

mcqs.q: A trial balance shows debit total ₹5,62,300 and credit total ₹5,58,800. The suspense account will show:
mcqs.explain: The credit side is short by ₹3,500, so suspense is credited with ₹3,500 to make the totals agree.

mcqs.q: Closing stock usually appears in the trial balance:
options: Only when it has already been adjusted against purchases
mcqs.explain: Normally closing stock is an adjustment outside the trial balance. If it has been adjusted through purchases, it appears on the debit side.

remarks: A frequent slip is putting the loan on the debit side because the money came into the bank — the loan itself is a liability.
Write the date in the heading: "Trial Balance as at …". Missing headings lose presentation marks.
mistakes: Showing interest received as a debit.
Forgetting drawings, which then inflates capital.
Calling the statement "Trial Balance for the year ended".
tips: List debits and credits in two passes so nothing is missed.
Show the capital working below the table.

questions.q: "Agreement of the trial balance is not a conclusive proof of accuracy of the books." Explain with examples.

model.text: A trial balance only proves that total debits equal total credits. Several errors keep this equality and therefore stay hidden:

items: Error of complete omission — a credit purchase never recorded: neither side is affected.
Wrong amount in the journal — ₹5,400 written as ₹4,500 and posted to both accounts.
Error of commission — cash received from Ajay credited to Vijay's account.
Error of principle — purchase of machinery debited to Purchases account.
Compensating errors — Sales account over-cast by ₹1,000 and Wages account over-cast by ₹1,000.

model.text: Hence an agreed trial balance shows arithmetical accuracy only; it does not prove that transactions were recorded correctly.

scheme.pt: Trial balance proves only arithmetical accuracy
At least three types of undisclosed errors named

remarks: Examples carry half the marks — a list of names without examples scores poorly.
mistakes: Including one-sided errors (which do affect the trial balance) in the list.
tips: Use "Error type — example" on each line.

summary: A trial balance lists ledger totals or balances on a date; the two columns must agree.
Debit: assets, expenses, losses, drawings. Credit: capital, liabilities, incomes, gains.
Agreement does not prove accuracy: omission, commission, principle and compensating errors stay hidden.
Unexplained differences go to suspense until rectified.
remember: It is a statement, not an account.
Outstanding expenses = credit; prepaid expenses = debit.
Closing stock is usually an adjustment outside the trial balance.
traps: Don't put a bank overdraft on the debit side.
Don't treat sales returns as income.
Don't say an agreed trial balance proves the books are correct.

viva.q: What is a trial balance and what are its objectives?
viva.model: A trial balance is a statement listing the balances or totals of all ledger accounts on a particular date. Its objectives are to check the arithmetical accuracy of posting and balancing, to give a summary of the ledger, and to serve as the base for preparing the financial statements.

points.pt: A statement of all ledger balances (or totals) on a particular date
Checks arithmetical accuracy of posting and balancing
Base for preparing final accounts / financial statements

viva.q: Name the methods of preparing a trial balance. Which one is used most?
viva.model: There are three methods: the total method, the balance method, and the total-cum-balance method. The balance method is the most commonly used, because final accounts are prepared from balances.

viva.model: No, agreement is not conclusive proof of accuracy. Several errors do not affect the agreement: an error of complete omission, an error of principle such as machinery debited to purchases, compensating errors that cancel each other, and an error of commission where the posting goes to the wrong account on the correct side.

viva.q: What is a suspense account and when is it opened?
viva.model: A suspense account is a temporary account opened when the trial balance does not agree and accounts must still be prepared. The difference is put into it so the totals agree for the time being. When the errors are found and rectified, the suspense account closes automatically.

points.pt: The trial balance difference is placed in it
It closes when the errors are rectified

cases.title: Asha's ledger balances on 31 March 2027
cases.case: Asha runs a small trading business. Her ledger shows these balances on 31 March 2027: Cash ₹18,000, Debtors ₹60,000, Purchases ₹1,50,000, Salaries ₹36,000, Furniture ₹50,000, Drawings ₹12,000, Sales returns ₹4,000, Rent ₹15,000, Bank overdraft ₹25,000, Creditors ₹42,000, Sales ₹2,40,000, Purchase returns ₹3,000. Her capital account balance is not given and is to be found as the balancing figure of the trial balance.

mcqs.q: What is the total of the debit column of the trial balance?
mcqs.explain: Debit balances: cash, debtors, purchases, salaries, furniture, drawings, sales returns and rent — they add up to ₹3,45,000.
Credit balances other than capital total ₹3,10,000. Capital = ₹3,45,000 − 3,10,000 = ₹35,000.

mcqs.q: On which side does the bank overdraft appear?
options: It is not shown in the trial balance
mcqs.explain: An overdraft means the business owes the bank, so it is a liability with a credit balance.

mcqs.q: Capital is entered at the figure found in the previous question. A clerk then shows sales returns of ₹4,000 on the credit side by mistake. By how much will the two totals differ?
mcqs.explain: The debit side loses 4,000 and the credit side gains 4,000 — a difference of twice the amount.
